name: Sample mean
variables: ybar = sample mean (estimate); y_j = observed values of the outcome Y; n = sample size. Uppercase Ybar denotes the estimator (a random variable), lowercase ybar its realised value.
notes: Basic building block; Ch 1–2 contain no worked numeric example.

name: Sampling distribution and standard error of the mean
expression: If Y ~ N(mu, sigma^2) then Ybar ~ N(mu, sigma^2/n);  SE(Ybar) = sigma_hat/sqrt(n) = s/sqrt(n)
variables: Y = outcome variable; mu = population mean; sigma = population SD; Ybar = sample mean; n = sample size; s = sigma_hat = sample SD; SE = standard error.
notes: conversions.sd_from_se implements the inverse direction (SD = SE·sqrt(n)), the usual data-extraction need.

name: Confidence interval for a mean
expression: (1 - alpha)·100% CI = ybar ± z_{alpha/2}·SE(Ybar) = ybar ± z_{alpha/2}·sigma_hat/sqrt(n);  LL = ybar - z_{alpha/2}·sigma_hat/sqrt(n),  UL = ybar + z_{alpha/2}·sigma_hat/sqrt(n)
variables: ybar = sample mean; z_{alpha/2} = upper alpha/2 point of N(0,1); sigma_hat = s = sample SD; n = sample size; LL, UL = lower and upper limits; alpha = significance level (0.05 for 95%).
notes: z-based (large-sample) interval; the exact small-sample CI would use t_{n-1}. effect_sizes.study_ci computes the generic Wald CI yi ± z·sqrt(vi).

name: Margin of error and CI width
expression: ME = z_{alpha/2}·sigma_hat/sqrt(n);  Width = UL - LL = 2·ME = 2·z_{alpha/2}·sigma_hat/sqrt(n)
variables: ME = margin of error; z_{alpha/2} = standard normal critical value; sigma_hat = sample SD; n = sample size; UL, LL = CI limits.
notes: Width increases with confidence level (90% z = 1.645; 95% z = 1.96) and variance, decreases with n. conversions.se_from_ci inverts this relation (SE = (UL - LL)/(2·z)) for data extraction.

name: Standard normal critical value
variables: Z ~ N(0,1); alpha = significance level; Phi^{-1} = standard normal quantile function.
notes: Source notes some people round 1.96 to 2.00 (a convention, not a computed value). The source uses 1.96 'by convention' for all meta-analysis CIs. norm_ppf(0.975) = 1.959964; norm_ppf(0.95) = 1.644854. [note: for random-effects pooled estimates the Cochrane Handbook v6 suggests considering a t-based HKSJ interval instead of the z-based one.]

name: z test statistic for a mean (sigma known)
expression: Z* = (Ybar - mu0) / (sigma/sqrt(n)) ~ N(0,1) under H0: mu = mu0
variables: Ybar = sample mean; mu0 = value under H0 (usually 0); sigma = known population SD; n = sample size.
notes: Two-sided alternative HA: mu != mu0, or one-sided upper-tailed HA: mu > mu0.

name: t test statistic for a mean (sigma estimated)
expression: T = (Ybar - mu0) / (sigma_hat/sqrt(n)) ~ t_{n-1} under H0
variables: Ybar = sample mean; mu0 = null value; sigma_hat = s = sample SD; n = sample size; t_{n-1} = Student t with n - 1 df.
notes: Exact under normality; the source then replaces it by the large-sample z approximation for n >= 30. The engine does not compute T itself; distributions.t_two_sided_p(T, n − 1) returns its two-sided p-value from the t_{n-1} distribution.

name: Large-sample z statistic used in meta-analysis
expression: Z = (Ybar - mu0) / (sigma_hat/sqrt(n)) approx ~ N(0,1) for n >= 30 (df >= 29)
variables: Ybar = sample mean; mu0 = null value; sigma_hat = sample SD; n = sample size.
notes: The source states that almost all meta-analyses use this approximation, citing the central limit theorem.

name: Two-sided p-value and decision rules
expression: p = P(|Z| >= |z0| given H0) = 2·[1 - Phi(|z0|)];  reject H0 if |z0| >= z_{alpha/2}  or equivalently if p <= alpha;  P(|Z| >= z_{alpha/2}) = alpha
variables: z0 = observed test statistic (Ybar - mu0)/(s/sqrt(n)); Phi = standard normal CDF; alpha = significance level; z_{alpha/2} = critical value.
notes: SOURCE ERROR: p. 21 prints P(|Z| >= z_{alpha/2}) = 1 - alpha and P(Z <= -z_{alpha/2}) + P(Z >= z_{alpha/2}) = 1 - alpha; the right-hand side should be alpha (equivalently P(|Z| <= z_{alpha/2}) = 1 - alpha). The source writes the p-value with '>' in one place and '>=' in the decision rule; the difference is immaterial for a continuous Z.

name: z test for a ratio measure on the log scale
expression: z = ln(theta_hat) / SE[ln(theta_hat)],  theta_hat = OR or RR
variables: theta_hat = estimated odds ratio or risk ratio; ln = natural logarithm; SE[ln theta_hat] = standard error on the log scale.
notes: Null value is 0 on the log scale (1 on the ratio scale). The pooled-estimate version is computed inside models.meta_analysis (stat = estimate/se) on log-scale yi.

name: Log-scale CI with back-transformation for ratio measures
expression: CI_ln = ln(theta_hat) ± 1.96·SE[ln(theta_hat)];  CI = [exp(ln(theta_hat) - 1.96·SE), exp(ln(theta_hat) + 1.96·SE)];  theta_hat = exp(ln theta_hat)
variables: theta_hat = OR or RR; SE = standard error of ln theta_hat; 1.96 = z_{0.025}; exp = exponential (back-transformation).
notes: Compute on the ln scale with effect_sizes.study_ci, then back-transform with effect_sizes.back_transform (exp for ratio measures). The back-transformed CI is asymmetric around theta_hat.

name: Log odds ratio to standardised mean difference
expression: d = ln(OR) × sqrt(3) / pi
variables: d = standardised mean difference; OR = odds ratio; pi = circle constant (3.14159...).
notes: Reconstructed from split text-box fragments [R]. The source writes pi = 22/7 (relative error about 0.04%); use math.pi. The source gives no variance conversion; the engine also returns V_d = V_lnOR·3/pi^2 (Borenstein et al. 2009). [note: assumes an underlying logistic distribution with equal variance in both groups (Cochrane Handbook v6 §10.6); document converted studies and test robustness by excluding them.]

name: Standardised mean difference to log odds ratio
expression: ln(OR) = d × pi / sqrt(3)
variables: d = standardised mean difference; OR = odds ratio; pi = circle constant.
notes: Reconstructed [R]. Use exact pi, not 22/7. Engine also returns V_lnOR = V_d·pi^2/3 (not in source).

name: Correlation to standardised mean difference
expression: d = 2r / sqrt(1 - r^2)
variables: d = standardised mean difference; r = Pearson correlation coefficient (|r| < 1).
notes: Reconstructed [R]. The source gives no d-to-r formula and no variance; conversions.r_to_d returns V_d = 4·V_r/(1 - r^2)^3 and conversions.d_to_r provides the reverse (Borenstein et al. 2009). [note: the factor 2 corresponds to equal group sizes; the general relation is d = sqrt(a)·r/sqrt(1 - r^2) with a = (n1 + n2)^2/(n1·n2), the inverse of conversions.d_to_r, and a = 4 when n1 = n2.]

name: Equal-weight (natural weight) arithmetic mean
expression: theta_bar = sum_{i=1}^{k} (1/k)·theta_hat_i
variables: theta_hat_i = effect estimate of study i; k = number of studies; 1/k = natural (equal) weight.
notes: Unbiased but not minimum-variance, so not used for pooling; RE estimates drift toward it when tau^2 is large.

name: Fixed-effect model, weights and pooled estimate
expression: theta_hat_i = theta + epsilon_i, epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma_i^2);  w_i = 1/v_i;  theta_hat_FE = sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i·theta_hat_i / sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i
variables: theta_hat_i = observed effect of study i; theta = common true effect; epsilon_i = within-study (sampling) error; sigma_i^2 = within-study variance estimated by v_i; w_i = inverse-variance weight; k = number of studies.
notes: Call models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='fixed'); CI is z-based as in the source.

name: Variance of the fixed-effect pooled estimate
expression: Var(theta_hat_FE) = ( sum_{i=1}^{k} 1/v_i )^{-1}
variables: v_i = within-study variance of study i; k = number of studies.
notes: The source warns this 'grossly underestimates' the actual variance under heterogeneity (inflated type I error). [note: do not choose FE because Q is non-significant; choose the model a priori (Cochrane Handbook v6 §10.10.4.1).]

name: Random-effects model and total study variance
expression: theta_hat_i = theta + zeta_i + epsilon_i,  zeta_i = theta_i - theta ~ N(0, tau^2),  epsilon_i = theta_hat_i - theta_i ~ N(0, sigma_i^2);  sigma_i*^2 = sigma_i^2 + tau^2 estimated by v_i* = v_i + tau_hat^2
variables: theta = mean of true effects; theta_i = true effect of study i; zeta_i = between-study deviation; epsilon_i = within-study error; tau^2 = between-study variance; tau_hat^2 = its estimate; v_i = within-study variance.
notes: No tau^2 estimator formula in Ch 1–2; DerSimonian & Laird 1986 is cited, implying DL. Engine: models.meta_analysis(model='random', tau2_method='DL'|'REML'|'PM'...); models.tau2_dl gives DL.

name: Random-effects weights, pooled estimate and variance
expression: w_i* = (v_i + tau_hat^2)^{-1};  theta_hat_RE = sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i*·theta_hat_i / sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i*;  Var(theta_hat_RE) = ( sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i* )^{-1}
variables: w_i* = random-effects weight; v_i = within-study variance; tau_hat^2 = estimated between-study variance; theta_hat_i = study estimate; k = number of studies.
notes: The source uses a z-based (Wald) CI. Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML/PM tau^2 and suggests considering HKSJ; the engine's default ci_method for random is 'hksj', so pass ci_method='z' and tau2_method='DL' to reproduce the classical DL analysis.

name: Intra-class correlation used by IVhet
expression: ICC_i = tau^2 / (tau^2 + v_i)
variables: tau^2 = between-study variance; v_i = within-study variance of study i.
notes: Interpretation from Kulinskaya & Olkin (2014). Not computed explicitly by the engine; implicit in models._ivhet.

name: IVhet quasi-likelihood scale parameter
expression: psi_i = sigma_i*^2 / v_i = (v_i + tau^2)/v_i = (1 - ICC_i)^{-1};  inflated variance contribution w_i^2·var(theta_hat_i)·psi_i
variables: psi_i = multiplicative over-dispersion scale parameter; sigma_i*^2 = total variance v_i + tau^2; v_i = within-study variance; ICC_i = intra-class correlation; w_i = normalised weight.
notes: Reconstructed from text-box fragments [R] (the source prints psi_i = v_i^{-1}·sigma_i^2 with garbled subscripts). Implicit in models._ivhet.

name: IVhet pooled estimate with normalised inverse-variance weights
expression: w_i = (1/v_i) / sum_{j=1}^{k} (1/v_j);  theta_hat_IVhet = sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i·theta_hat_i  (= theta_hat_FE)
variables: w_i = normalised inverse-variance weight (weights sum to 1); v_i = within-study variance; theta_hat_i = study estimate; k = number of studies.
notes: Reconstructed [R]. Public entry point: models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='ivhet'). The point estimate is identical to the fixed-effect estimate.

name: IVhet variance of the pooled estimate
expression: Var(theta_hat_IVhet) = sum_{i=1}^{k} [ (1/v_i) / sum_{j=1}^{k} (1/v_j) ]^2 · (v_i + tau_hat^2)
variables: v_i = within-study variance; tau_hat^2 = estimated between-study variance; k = number of studies.
notes: Reconstructed [R]. The source does not name the tau^2 estimator; Doi et al. 2015a/MetaXL and the engine use DerSimonian–Laird (models.tau2_dl). CI = estimate ± 1.96·sqrt(Var) is inferred from the book's z convention; the engine uses z. [note: IVhet is its developers' proposal, not a Cochrane default; present it as an alternative or sensitivity analysis.]

name: Quality-score rescaling for the QE model
expression: Q_i = score_i / max_j(score_j)
variables: score_i = methodological quality score of study i; max_j(score_j) = highest score in the meta-analysis; Q_i in [0, 1].
notes: From the Doi et al. 2015b update: scores become relative to the best study. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Quality-effects (QE) model weights and pooled estimate
expression: theta_hat_QE = sum_{i=1}^{k} w'_i·theta_hat_i,  w'_i = (Q_i/v_i + tau_hat_i) / sum_{j=1}^{k} (Q_j/v_j + tau_hat_j)
variables: Q_i = rescaled quality score (0–1); v_i = within-study variance; tau_hat_i = quality-based weight-redistribution term (NOT the between-study variance tau^2), defined in Doi et al. 2015b Appendix A; w'_i = modified weight; theta_hat_i = study estimate.
notes: Reconstructed [R]. The variance of theta_hat_QE and the definition of tau_hat_i are not reproduced in the book (see Doi et al. 2015b Appendix A). With equal quality the QE estimator reduces to IVhet. Not implemented in the engine. [note: the Cochrane Handbook v6 advises against weighting by quality scores; prefer restriction to low risk-of-bias studies or stratified/sensitivity analyses.]

name: Cochran's Q statistic (computational form)
expression: Q = sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i·theta_hat_i^2 - ( sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i·theta_hat_i )^2 / sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i,  w_i = 1/v_i
variables: w_i = fixed-effect inverse-variance weight; theta_hat_i = study estimate; v_i = within-study variance; k = number of studies.
notes: Algebraically equal to sum w_i·(theta_hat_i - theta_hat_FE)^2, which models.cochran_q computes (numerically more stable). The source misspells it 'Cochrane's Q'.

name: Null distribution and p-value of the Q test
expression: Under H0: theta_1 = ... = theta_k,  Q ~ chi^2_{k-1};  p = P(chi^2_{k-1} >= Q)
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; df = k - 1; chi^2 = chi-squared distribution (right-skewed, df only parameter).
notes: models.heterogeneity returns p_Q via distributions.chi2_sf. The source notes Q grows with the number of studies; the test has low power with few studies. [note: do not base the FE/RE choice on this test (Cochrane Handbook v6 §10.10.4.1).]

name: I-squared heterogeneity statistic
expression: I^2 = (Q - df)/Q × 100%,  df = k - 1;  standard practice: I^2 = max(0, (Q - df)/Q) × 100%
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = degrees of freedom; k = number of studies.
notes: The source prints the formula without truncation at 0, so it can give negative values when Q < df; the engine truncates at 0. No interpretation thresholds or CI are given in Ch 1–2. [note: if interpreted, use the Cochrane Handbook v6 overlapping bands (0–40%, 30–60%, 50–90%, 75–100%) as rough guides, not absolute cut-offs; I^2 rises with study precision, so report it with its CI and tau^2.]

name: Wald (z-based) confidence interval and z-test for a pooled estimate
expression: CI = theta_hat ± z_{alpha/2}·sqrt(Var(theta_hat));  z = theta_hat / sqrt(Var(theta_hat));  p = 2·[1 - Phi(|z|)];  z_{0.025} = 1.96
variables: theta_hat = pooled estimate (FE, RE or IVhet; on the log scale for ratio measures); Var(theta_hat) = its model-based variance; z_{alpha/2} = standard normal critical value; Phi = standard normal CDF.
notes: Assembled from the source's statements that the CI and test for the pooled effect use the standard normal critical value and that 1.96 is used for all meta-analysis CIs by convention. Engine: models.meta_analysis(..., ci_method='z'), the default for model='fixed'; model='ivhet' always uses z. [note: for random effects the Cochrane Handbook v6 suggests considering the t-based HKSJ interval (ci_method='hksj', the engine default for model='random') and reporting a prediction interval, neither of which the source covers.]
